trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out to (6,4,7) or to (4,6,7) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (6,4,7).
I can't rule out to (6,2,7) or to (7,4,6) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (6,2,7).
Going to (7,2,6) would leave number 3 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (4,2,7).
I can't rule out to (2,2,7) or to (4,1,6) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (2,2,7).
I can't rule out to (1,2,6) or to (2,1,6) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (1,2,6).
Going to (1,4,6) would force the line onto number 20 before its turn; going to (2,1,6) would leave number 4 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (1,2,4).
Number 4 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
I can't rule out to (2,1,2) or to (2,2,1) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (2,1,2).
Number 5 is only reachable this way.
The line must go to (2,1,6): to (4,1,4) is number 15, which comes later.
Going to (7,2,4) would leave number 7 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (7,4,6).
Number 7 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
I can't rule out to (6,6,7) or to (7,6,4) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (6,6,7).
The line must go to (4,6,7): to (6,7,6) is number 9, which comes later.
Going to (2,6,7) would force the line onto number 20 before its turn. So the line goes to (4,7,6).

Going to (2,7,6) would strand number 9: it would be left with only one free neighbour; going to (4,7,4) would strand number 9: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes to (6,7,6).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (6,7,4).

Going to (4,7,4) would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order); going to (6,7,2) would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order). So the line goes to (7,6,4).
Number 10 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going to (7,4,2) would force the line onto number 12 before its turn; going to (6,6,1) leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes to (6,7,2).
The line must go to (6,6,1): to (4,7,2) is number 18, which comes later.
Going to (6,4,1) leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes to (4,6,1).
Going to (2,6,1) leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes to (4,4,1).
Going to (2,4,1) would cut off a group of 12 cells. So the line goes to (6,4,1).
Going to (6,2,1) would leave number 12 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (7,4,2).
Number 12 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going to (6,1,2) would leave both number 14 and cell (6,2,1) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes to (6,2,1).
The line must go to (6,1,2): to (4,2,1) is number 16, which comes later.
Going to (4,1,2) would leave both number 15 and number 16 needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes to (6,1,4).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (4,1,4).
Going to (2,6,1), the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (1,6,2). So the line goes to (1,4,2).
The line must go to (1,6,2): to (1,4,4) is number 21, which comes later.
Cell (2,6,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (2,7,2).
Going to (2,7,4) would strand number 18: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes to (4,7,2).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (4,7,4).
Going to (2,7,6) leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes to (1,6,4).
Number 19 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Cell (2,7,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (2,6,7).
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
I grow a search tree: my policy network suggests moves, a trained value head judge them. 56 simulations per move.
One of my simulated futures reached the end after 6 simulations. Following it!
Let evolution do the work: 24 random lines compete, the fittest breed and mutate.
Generation 0: the best random line covers 23/54 cells (43%).
Generation 1: fitness 47/54. The best line covers 52 cells, the first 47 of them still look solvable.
Generation 2: fitness 54/54. The best line covers 54 cells.
Generation 2: a perfect line evolved! Every cell covered.
Feeling lucky! Before every move I'll play 24 random futures and bet on the move that survives most often.
Tried 72 futures: 8% survive going to (6,4,7) (best covers 87%); to (4,2,7) 4%; to (4,6,7) 0%.
Tried 72 futures: 4% survive going to (6,2,7) (best covers 54%); to (7,4,6) 0%; to (6,6,7) 0%.
Tried 48 futures: 0% survive going to (4,2,7) (best covers 15%); to (7,2,6) 0%.
Tried 48 futures: 8% survive going to (2,2,7) (best covers 50%); to (4,1,6) 0%.
Tried 48 futures: 4% survive going to (1,2,6) (best covers 33%); to (2,1,6) 0%.
Jackpot! A future after going to (1,2,4) covers the whole board. Cashing in!
